title: Dev log: evidence board and plain language
author: claude
summary: The dev log now opens on a cork evidence board, and every entry is written in plain English.
what: We added a board view to the dev log and made it the first page you see. It looks like a detective's evidence board: a cork background, cards pinned on it, and red string. The old timeline is still there as a second tab. We also rewrote every entry in plain language and sorted them into topics, steps and sub-tasks.
why: A long list is hard to follow. The board shows what belongs together, what came after what, and what had to be done first. Plain words mean a client can follow the story too.
how:
- Topics run left to right, the steps of each topic run top to bottom in the order they were done, and sub-tasks hang beside their step.
- Solid arrows say "then", dashed blue arrows say "needed first", and red strings join related cards.
- Click a card to light up its branch and open the details beside the board.
- Dragging a card saves its place; "Reset layout" puts everything back.
beforeText: A single list of entries, newest first, with technical wording.
afterText: A board of topics, steps and sub-tasks with arrows and strings, and plain-language detail pages.
wrong: Two early layout problems: a header style on the page also hit the board's corner panels and hid the top row of cards, and the step cards of one column drifted sideways and overlapped.
fix: The header class was renamed, and every column is now laid out as one straight stack after dagre has placed it.
next: Check the form's drag-and-drop and paste in a real browser session.

tech.name: React Flow
tech.plain: Draws the board and lets you zoom, pan and drag the cards.

tech.name: dagre
tech.plain: Works out where each card goes, top to bottom, so nothing has to be placed by hand.

tech.name: Auto-layout
tech.plain: The computer places the cards; only cards you move yourself are remembered.
